title: If Dogs Eat Chocolate: 9 mg/lb Theobromine Can Cause Mild Signs 🍫 (Things Living In Your House #72)
description:
Can dogs eat chocolate? No: the FDA says chocolate is toxic to dogs. The FDA says theobromine can cause mild signs in dogs with doses as low as 9 mg per pound of body weight, and severe signs starting around 18 mg per pound. It is per pound of the dog, so a small dog needs less chocolate to get there. In the FDA's table, dark chocolate with 70-85% cacao has about 227 mg of theobromine per ounce and milk chocolate about 57 mg, so about 4 times as much. If your dog ate chocolate or seems sick, call your veterinarian; if your vet is unavailable, the FDA says to call an emergency animal hospital or an animal poison control center. General information, not advice for your dog.

#dogs #chocolate #meatballmyths #shorts

Sources: U.S. FDA, Animal Health Literacy page on chocolate and dogs (fda.gov); ASPCA Animal Poison Control, people foods to avoid feeding your pets (aspca.org).
